text: Astronomers view distant celestial objects with telescopes, employing sophisticated instruments to capture light from sources that are either too distant or too faint for the naked eye to perceive. These telescopes range from large, professional models such as the Hubble Space Telescope, offering stunning images of distant galaxies and nebulae, to smaller, portable units like those used for astrophoto contests. Telescopes capture images by focusing light through lenses or mirrors, enhancing it to resolve fine details. The advancement of technology in telescope design, including improvements in optics, detectors, and data processing, continually enhances their capabilities, allowing astronomers to probe deeper into the universe and uncover secrets of its formation and evolution. The ability of telescopes to view the cosmos in various wavelengths, from radio waves to gamma rays, provides a comprehensive view of celestial phenomena. As telescopes continue to push the boundaries of what we can see and understand, they play a pivotal role in astrophysics, driving scientific discovery and advancing our understanding of the universe.
summary: Astronomers view distant celestial objects with telescopes.
